articles.title: Remote Access by Default: Auditing the Plex Port Forwards That Made Plex2Shell Exploitable
articles.excerpt: Remote Access by Default: Auditing the Plex Port Forwards That Made Plex2Shell Exploitable Every account of the Plex2Shell campaign boils down to the same precondition: the server had to be reachable.…
articles.body: Remote Access by Default: Auditing the Plex Port Forwards That Made Plex2Shell Exploitable Every account of the Plex2Shell campaign boils down to the same precondition: the server had to be reachable. The vulnerability chain, comprising CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655 and CVE-2026-96656, is only exploitable from outside if requests arrive from outside. That makes network configuration the highest-leverage control an administrator has, and the one most likely to be undocumented. This article treats the exposure question as an audit problem rather than a patching problem. What the vulnerable state looks like Plex Media Server before 1.43.3.10861 is affected.

articles.title: Ghost in the Machine 👻: Creating Ghost Stories with Local AI

articles.body: 👻 Ghost in the Machine What if the machine in your room could tell you a ghost story without sending your prompt to a hosted AI API? This is my submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge — Week 4: Ghost in the Machine . What I Built Ghost in the Machine is a local AI-powered ghost story generator. Users enter a prompt and the application generates a spooky story using the Gemma 3 1B model through Ollama. I built this project to explore how open-weight AI models can power creative applications on a local machine. The project combines a React and TypeScript frontend with an Express backend and local AI inference.

articles.title: Shipping Flutter Web to Firebase When Your GitHub Actions Budget Hits Zero
articles.excerpt: On October 18, right in the middle of shipping a multi-feature audit and a supplement tracker redesign on my personal life_os_app (my daily Flutter Web + Cloud Firestore operating board), GitHub Actio…
articles.body: On October 18, right in the middle of shipping a multi-feature audit and a supplement tracker redesign on my personal life_os_app (my daily Flutter Web + Cloud Firestore operating board), GitHub Actions stopped scheduling jobs. The billing meter for my personal account's hosted runner minutes had hit 100%. Look at what my .github/workflows/ci.yml and deploy-live.yml were doing on every push and pull request: Spinning up an ubuntu-latest VM. Pulling the Flutter SDK and warming the Pub cache (~90s). Installing Python 3 and running 68 CLI sync unit tests (~15s). Running flutter analyze and 466 widget and accessibility tests (~110s). Compiling flutter build web --release --no-web-resources-cdn (~140s).

articles.title: I compared native vs middleware costs for 55 B2B integrations. Middleware wins on paper 13 times — and that's the trap
articles.excerpt: Every "connect X to Y" page shows you the happy path. Almost none of them tell you which plan tier the native connector actually requires, or what happens to your bill when you route the same integrat…
articles.body: Every "connect X to Y" page shows you the happy path. Almost none of them tell you which plan tier the native connector actually requires, or what happens to your bill when you route the same integration through middleware instead. I built an open index of 55 B2B integrations with exactly that math: the minimum plan tier each native connector requires, the API and webhook gates behind it, and a middleware alternative priced the same way (cheapest API-capable tiers plus about $9/month for Make). All of it is calculated for a 10-seat team, from verified vendor pricing pages. The full index is at https://stackcostmatrix.com — and the dataset is open on GitHub. Here is what the comparison actually shows.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 27 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Noctilucent Clouds over Sweden Explanation: Sometimes it’s night on the ground but day in the air. As the Earth rotates to eclipse the Sun, sunset rises up from the ground. Therefore, at sunset on the ground, sunlight still shines on clouds above. Under usual circumstances , a pretty sunset might be visible, but unusual noctilucent clouds float so high up they can be seen well after dark.

articles.title: Analog astronauts: How living underwater can prepare humans for space missions
articles.excerpt: How living underwater can prepare humans for space missions
articles.body: I have been dreaming of doing research in space as an astronaut my whole life, but for some reason, the thought of working underwater made me nervous. I’ve known for a long time that astronauts train underwater to simulate different scenarios they’re likely to experience in space. Diving was never an issue for me, either — I even made it as far as becoming a certified rescue diver. So what was the problem? This summer, I led a simulated space mission in an underwater habitat called the Jules’ Undersea Lab. It is a research station that is located 22 feet (6.7 meters) underwater near Key Largo, Florida. You have to scuba dive to get in and out of the station. To become an aquanaut , you have to stay underwater for at least 24 hours in a so-called state of saturation.
